text:
You need Apple Pay and Google Pay embedded into an existing working Tranzila iframe on a WordPress site, including the Apple merchant authentication file setup and testing before go-live.

I’m Tobias Reyne, a full-stack developer with 7 years of experience working with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. I’ve worked on integrations where the key challenge was making real-time or payment-related functionality fit cleanly into an existing system without disrupting what already works.

One project that’s relevant is the Live fleet dashboard I built for Ferrylane Freight. It was a dispatcher map that showed every truck’s position and ETA, with updates pushed to the browser as GPS pings arrived. The result was 1,800 trucks tracked live with under 2 seconds from ping to screen. That project required careful handling of live data flow, browser-side behavior, and reliable integration across the stack — the same kind of attention I’d bring to your Tranzila/WordPress payment setup.

For your job, I’d focus on:
- embedding the Apple Pay JS/library file in the required `.well-known` location
- making sure the Tranzila jQuery integration is properly loaded inside the iframe
- checking the Apple Pay and Google Pay flow end to end in the existing WordPress environment
- validating the setup before go-live so the payment experience is stable and consistent

I’m comfortable working inside an existing codebase and following the exact constraints of a hosted payment flow, especially when the implementation needs to work within a specific iframe structure. Since this is already a working site, I’d approach it carefully: verify the current Tranzila integration, confirm the asset placement requirements, test the payment buttons and callbacks, and then help you get it ready for production.

If you’d like, I can take this on and work through the integration step by step.
